speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long this has been present and if you have any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The patient's history of an ant bite (likely sand fly), the ulcerative nature of the lesion, and the immunocompromised state from Crohn's disease and steroid use strongly supports this diagnosis over simple cellulitis or a spider bite.
